reviews.comment: Study guides were provided before exams, but they did not help in terms of when it came to the exams. Lots of slides on the actual material. Gave pre-quizzes. 3 exams, not cumulative, but has an optional final exam that is cumulative, which can help if you did badly on any exams. No extra credit and no curves on exams.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took him for a summer session for 433 not 427 it just wasn't a listed option. Amazing professor, would recommend him for sure.
This is one of the best professors I have ever taken. Thank you, Mr. Riechman.

I liked this professor as he promoted critical thinking. His exams are difficult but he always curves them. I found the class interesting and the professor was clearly knowledgable on the subject. He also joked with us throughout the semester. For exams, just study your lecture notes (what's said in class) and the textbook.
curve is good, but no extra credit and too much material to cram. Would not take this class in a million years

Dont take him unless you are very confident in your test taking abilities. It was around 30 very difficult concept questions from a minimum of 70 FILLED slides. If you have to take him, dont go to class. Just study every little thing on the slides. An A is possible but work hard for the first exam. He curves well but dont count on it.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: In terms of knowledge he is very smart, but as a teacher he doesn't correlate the material to what you will be tested over well. There is no textbook and you are given generic slides that are overly filled with information. Doesn't believe in multiple-choice so does A and B are correct-type questions that are poorly worded. Would not recommend.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's really nice, but he wastes a lot of time in class, and I felt that he did a very poor job connecting what he was teaching to genuine therapeutic principles (the course's namesake). Also, the slides he teaches off of are a horrible, overfilled mess, which bothered me a lot. It won't be the end of the world if you take him. Can't recommend tho..

This class will leave you wanting more of the info he provides. His passion for the material being taught truly comes out and he does rant a lot about many things. The tests weren't too bad and there is an easy group project at the end. A very nice person who is serious about the material, he encourages dialogue in class and loves hearing feedback
